title: KV-Repurpose: A Testbed for Evaluating Non-Prefix KV-Cache Reuse
summary: Replaces exact-prefix KV-cache reuse with segment-wise reuse, allowing cached document blocks to be reused across different system prompts and conversation histories in a vLLM-based serving stack. Costs include adopting and maintaining a custom scheduling, prompt-construction, and capacity-management layer on top of vLLM, plus engineering effort to segment workloads correctly. Naive segment reuse largely preserves quality on single-document QA and summarization, but the paper reports clear degradation in cross-document reasoning, and the reported gains are demonstrated only under a specific Zipfian RAG workload, so real traffic may benefit far less.
rationale: The approach is directly relevant to RAG serving on constrained infrastructure and shows large TTFT gains, but it is an early testbed whose quality regressions and workload dependence require validation on the reader's own traffic before production adoption.

claims.statement: Replaces exact-prefix KV-cache reuse with segment-wise reuse, allowing cached document blocks to be reused across different system prompts and conversation histories in a vLLM-based serving stack. Costs include adopting and maintaining a custom scheduling, prompt-construction, and capacity-management layer on top of vLLM, plus engineering effort to segment workloads correctly. Naive segment reuse largely preserves quality on single-document QA and summarization, but the paper reports clear degradation in cross-document reasoning, and the reported gains are demonstrated only under a specific Zipfian RAG workload, so real traffic may benefit far less.

Under a Zipfian RAG workload with 20% of requests sharing a fixed prefix, token-level cache hit rate rises to 63.9% versus 3.3% for prefix caching at the same 30 GB capacity (prefix caching reaches only 17.9% even with 1 TB), resulting in lower TTFT.
